chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to a man from the Ansar: 'When you have pelted the Jamarat, there would be for you with each pebble (pelted), ten good deeds being written for you for whatever is from your life in the future'.

key_terms.الْأَنْصَارِ: The Helpers, the native inhabitants of Medina who supported the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).
key_terms.الْجِمَارَ: The Jamarat (pillars/stones) in Mina, symbolizing the rejection of Satan, which are stoned during Hajj.
key_terms.حَسَنَاتٍ: Good deeds or rewards recorded in the heavenly book.
key_terms.حَصَاةٍ: A small pebble or stone used for the ritual stoning.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for throwing pebbles at the Jamarat during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the spiritual merit of the Rami al-Jamarat ritual, linking the physical act of stoning the pillars to a cumulative reward of ten good deeds per pebble that extends throughout the pilgrim's remaining lifespan. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted as a divine encouragement for the Ansar and later pilgrims to maintain the Sunnah of the Prophet, emphasizing the continuity of reward (sadaqah jariyah) for acts of worship performed with intention. The narration underscores the transformative power of the Hajj rituals, where a simple physical action becomes a vessel for enduring spiritual accumulation.
